thread:
maya: hitting a weird JSON.parse error when consuming SSE from the hosted API. only happens on long responses with emojis — parser fails mid-stream

alex: emoji = multibyte. are you sure your client handles split UTF-8 boundaries? Node TextDecoder has streaming mode.

maya: hmm could be. stack shows 'Unexpected end of JSON input' right after an emoji in the chunk boundary. using fetch + body.getReader() and assembling strings.

jim: if you're concat-ing strings you can accidentally split surrogate pairs too. recommended: work in bytes and use TextDecoder.decode(chunk, {stream: true}) so decoder preserves partial multibyte seqs.

maya: can you paste a tiny snippet?

alex: sure, node-ish example:
```js
const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8');
let text = '';
while(true) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  text += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
  // try to extract complete JSON frames here
}
text += decoder.decode(); // flush
```

srini: for Python use codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')() — same idea: feed bytes, it buffers incomplete sequences. also don't naive-split on newlines if SSE event 'data:' may be chunked.

jim: another angle is backpressure: if your consumer is slow and you keep accepting reads you may accumulate large buffers and then try to parse partial JSON. best to pause/resume the source or apply a max-buffer threshold and signal upstream. in Node streams, reader.cancel() or reader.releaseLock() are options depending on implementation.

maya: what's a pragmatic max-buffer? our messages can be ~150KB at peak.

jim: try 1MB hard cap for safety, but prefer incremental parsing: only parse once you detect a full SSE event (blank line terminator) or well-formed NDJSON line. don't wait for entire payload if protocol guarantees frames.

alex: we should update SDK examples to show streaming-safe patterns: TextDecoder streaming, incremental JSON parser (toy: try JSON.parse when you see matching braces count or newline-delimited frames), and backpressure knobs.

srini: quick python snippet:
```py
from codecs import getincrementaldecoder
dec = getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
buf = b''
while True:
  chunk = await resp.content.read(8192)
  if not chunk:
    break
  s = dec.decode(chunk)
  # accumulate lines and detect complete events
```

maya: deploy-bot just noted a deploy around the time I started hitting this — could be unrelated but throwing it in here: deploy-bot: stage/api-gw v2.14.1 -> SUCCESS

deply-bot? (typo)

deploy-bot: thanks — noted. no streaming changes in that deploy, mainly auth header rotation.

maya: one more: reconnect semantics. if we reconnect mid-stream can we resume with last-event-id?

alex: SSE supports Last-Event-ID header; server has to emit id: on events. recommend clients store last id from 'id:' field and include 'Last-Event-ID' on reconnect. fallback: incremental dedupe on server side.

jim: for SDK default behavior: expose three knobs — decoder (auto for utf-8), maxBufferBytes, and maxInFlightEvents. default maxBufferBytes=1_048_576, maxInFlightEvents=50, retryBackoff=exponential(500ms). sounds reasonable?

srini: +1. add sample for handling partial JSON object: keep a small ring buffer of trailing bytes up to 8, decode with stream true, then only attempt JSON.parse when braces balance or newline terminator seen.

maya: great, I'll try switching to TextDecoder streaming and add a simple brace-balance check before parse. will report back. thanks all :thumbsup:
